Pull Request Security Review

Execution trace of the multi-agent security pipeline auditing PR #8 in the chai-com repository. Findings are processed via AI correlation to filter noise and prioritize SRE remediations prior to merging.

Authorashok-yannam
Target Systemchai-com on Kubernetes
TriggerGitHub Workflow

Executive Summary

The chai-com workload exhibits a compounded risk profile within the multi-tenant cluster. Application-level vulnerabilities (DOM XSS, SSRF) act as direct stepping stones to critical cluster infrastructure due to a lack of network isolation and overly permissive cloud IAM roles. An unauthenticated external attacker can achieve full cloud account takeover in a single attack chain.

01. Context Ingestion: Design & PRD Review

Agent Severity Finding & Threat Details & Impact
Design Review HIGH Missing Auth Rotation Authentication relies on a single HS256 JWT without rotation, violating the "strong authentication" design standard.
Impact: Long-term persistence if key is leaked.
Design Review HIGH Missing Namespace Boundary No defined trust boundary between the workload namespace and kube-system. Assumes single-tenant isolation but deploys to shared cluster.
Impact: Lateral movement across tenant boundaries.

02. Code Analysis

Agent Severity Finding & Threat Details, PoC & Impact
SAST Agent CRIT SQL Injection (Auth Bypass)
T1190		 Constructs queries via string concatenation in routes/search.ts, allowing an attacker to bypass authentication.
PoC: POST /rest/user/login {"email":"' OR 1=1--"}
Impact: Full database dump including PII/PCI.
SAST Agent CRIT Server-Side Request Forgery
T1552.005		 Unvalidated URL parameter in routes/profileImageUrl.ts allows internal network probing.
Impact: Access to internal APIs and Cloud Metadata.
Secrets Agent CRIT Committed Cloud Creds
T1552.001		 Active AWS Access Key ID and Secret Access Key committed in .env.example.
Impact: Instant cloud account compromise by repository scanners.

Correlation & Validation: Code Scanning

The AI engine merged the SAST SSRF finding and the committed AWS Key into a verified application-layer exploit chain.

SRE Runbook: Immediate Remediation

  • Revoke Keys: In AWS IAM Console, revoke the compromised Access Key immediately and remove from .env.example.
  • Fix SSRF: In routes/profileImageUrl.ts, implement an allowed domain list and explicitly block IP resolution to 169.254.169.254.

03. IaC & Pipeline

Agent Severity Finding & Threat Details, PoC & Impact
Terraform Agent CRIT IMDSv1 Enabled on Node
T1552.005		 EKS node group allows IMDSv1 queries without a session token (http_tokens = "optional").
PoC: fetch('http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/')
Impact: Pods with SSRF can extract Node IAM credentials.
Helm Agent CRIT Privileged Container Escape
T1611		 Deployment runs the container with securityContext.privileged: true, runAsUser: 0, and hostPID: true.
PoC: nsenter --target 1 --mount --uts --ipc --net --pid
Impact: Container escape to underlying worker node as root.

Correlation & Validation: Code + Infra

Mapped the application-layer SSRF directly to the Terraform-provisioned IMDSv1 nodes, confirming an escalation path from the container to Cloud IAM.

SRE Runbook: Immediate Remediation

  • Patch Manifest: In helm/charts/chai-com/templates/deployment.yaml, set privileged: false and readOnlyRootFilesystem: true.
  • Enforce IMDSv2: In terraform/eks-nodes.tf, update the launch template: metadata_options { http_tokens = "required" }.

04. Cloud & Cluster Posture

Agent Severity Finding & Threat Details, PoC & Impact
Cloud Config CRIT Over-Permissive Node IAM
T1078.004		 IAM role attached to worker nodes possesses s3:* wildcard permissions.
Impact: Broad data exfiltration (2.1M records) from any compromised node.
K8s Security CRIT Unauth Kubelet API
T1609		 The Kubelet allows anonymous-auth on port 10250, bypassing RBAC.
PoC: curl -X POST https://[NODE_IP]:10250/run/kube-system/tiller/c1 -d "cmd=id"
Impact: Remote Code Execution in any cluster pod (including kube-system).

Correlation & Validation: Cloud Posture

Connecting the permissive Node IAM role to the unauth kubelet verified that node compromise equals total cloud account and cluster compromise.

SRE Runbook: Immediate Remediation

  • Lock Kubelet: Edit /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml on nodes: set authentication.anonymous.enabled: false.
  • Restrict IAM: In terraform/iam.tf, replace s3:* with a scoped policy targeting required ARNs.

05 & 06. Defense & Paved Path

Agent Severity Finding & Threat Details & Impact
Standards HIGH Missing Network Isolation
T1021		 No default-deny NetworkPolicy exists. East-west traffic is completely unrestricted across the cluster.
Impact: Seamless lateral movement for attackers.
Product Def. HIGH Missing CSP Header
T1059.007		 No Content-Security-Policy header is emitted, leaving the DOM XSS vulnerabilities highly exploitable.
Impact: Silent session hijacking via XSS payloads.

Correlation & Validation: Defense Deficiencies

The lack of NetworkPolicies combined with the lack of CSP means attackers face zero friction traversing from the browser to the backend network.

SRE Runbook: Immediate Remediation

  • Isolate Network: Create k8s/network-policy.yaml with DefaultDeny, allowing inbound only from Ingress.
  • Add Header: In server.ts, append Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'.

07. Validation & Attack Path Analysis

The Red Team agent utilized the aggregated pipeline findings to autonomously execute CHN-KILL-01 in the staging environment. Total time to cluster-admin was 2 hours and 47 minutes.
